description: CONTRACT change of an already consumed block event, on top of job:block-events-reactive: OnRate gains the parameter RatedAt and becomes mandatory (IsMandatory true). It proves what happens to whoever already consumed it: the screen instance keeps the SAME handler key, the new argument is born empty in the consumer (the get of the IEventHandler shows Arguments 3) and has to be filled in on both sides - in the producer (the ITriggerNode) and in the consumer (the new input of the handler) - otherwise Verify refuses with RequiredPropertyValue_Value; mandatory does not break whoever already had a handler linked.

ops._why: state before: the trigger of the block and the handler of the screen

ops.name: RatedAt
ops._why: 1. add a parameter to the contract
2. make the event mandatory for whoever instantiates the block
the producer already sees 3 arguments; the new one is still to be filled in
the consumer keeps the handler key and now has 3 arguments, the new one empty
3. migrate the producer: whoever triggers now sends the new value

ops.name: LastRatedAt
ops._why: 4. migrate the consumer: the handler receives and uses the new parameter
o argumento do handler, no escopo do evento
5. the screen uses the new data, otherwise the parameter is left unused
new contract: 3 parameters and IsMandatory True
after the migration: the SAME handler key, now with the 3 arguments filled in
state after: the same two consumers, none lost
